The empty list has the vacuous choice v=0 and no fractional partition because P is nonempty. For h=1 it is always empty since every nonempty proper face omits a positive-weight vertex. The mixed strict conclusion correctly assumes h>1, including for the full minimal face.

One small positive ε simultaneously preserves all weights, total M, and the strict subcritical status of every original subcritical subset, by finiteness of P. Every originally critical proper face becomes subcritical. A center for w′ is a center for w because each closed halfspace trace is a subset of P. Thus none of the small original proper faces contains the center, while the full face weighs M>α.

The affine transfer is applied to the original positive fibers and original atomic weights at the selected site. The auxiliary weights are used only for center selection. The strict statement concerns an actual centroid mark; equality of the maximum then implies the partition. No sufficiency of a fractional partition is claimed.

For a site q outside all small proper faces, e_q−w/M has sum zero and gives −α/M on each critical face. A relative-interior site is outside every nonempty proper face. In the complete integer case the constant graph satisfies same-parity midpoint closure and has exactly the base traces of product lifts. For positive-volume fibers of a convex body, at a lattice point in the hull of their bases the fiber contains a Minkowski convex combination, which contains a positive scaling of any participating full-dimensional fiber with nonzero coefficient, translated by chosen points from the others.

overlap.comparison: Its proof before incidence classes already proves the unrestricted separation/fractional-balance step by the same constant-vector argument, with its k replaceable by h there. The stated theorem assumes midpoint labels and derives the stronger singleton-vertex classification at M/k. It does not prove strict actual mixed depth for affine fibers at an arbitrary supplied Helly bound.

It gives excess minimal-face mass for a weighted atomic center under midpoint-label closure at M/k except for the equal-weight vertex case. The present theorem uses a fractional obstruction at supplied M/h without such label closure and transfers strictness to actual fiber depth.
Its affine-centroid corollary gives the weak ≥γ_d M/2^n bound for actual lattice fibers. It supplies neither a strictness criterion nor a necessary fractional partition for equality.
